documents.title: Using Generative AI at Colby College - A Legal Perspective (guidance memorandum)
documents.stance_why: The memo sets no course or academic-use rule; it says its considerations "should not discourage you from exploring and using artificial intelligence" and attaches tips and conditions (verify output, disclose, protect data, use approved tools). With disclosure and data limits on an otherwise allowed use, it is permit rather than encourage or delegates.
documents.summary: A general counsel memo to all Colby users of generative AI covering privacy, hiring bias, hallucination, IP, antitrust and cybercrime risks, followed by practical guidelines on verifying and disclosing AI use and avoiding AI for critical decisions. It gives little classroom-specific direction and points to the Davis Institute, CTL and Provost for academic questions.

units.why: The memo opens by framing its purpose: "thoughtful guidance that goes beyond the classroom" for navigating generative AI, which sets scope and principles for the whole community, so I use the institution-wide framework type rather than a definition.
units.anchor: Our aim is to provide thoughtful guidance that goes beyond the classroom

units.why: Explains what generative AI is ("does not 'know' facts. It predicts"), setting what the guidance covers; a definition so P61, not P31, though it implies unreliability.
units.anchor: it does not "know" facts. It predicts what to produce or generate
units.frag_end: patterns it has seen or been provided

units.why: States that outputs "can be biased, outdated, or inaccurate", a caution about AI output reliability; P31 fits better than P53 because it is about output quality for the user.
units.anchor: the output it produces can be biased, outdated, or inaccurate

units.why: The memo says its considerations "should not discourage you from exploring and using artificial intelligence", an affirmative default welcoming use, so P02.
units.anchor: discourage you from exploring and using artificial intelligence

units.why: The Key Takeaway calls generative AI "a powerful tool with significant potential to enhance our work", a pro-use principle, P02.

notes: Only one college-level document; legal guidance, not an academic-use policy. Several units are UNCOVERED (critical decisions about people, antitrust, cybercrime, cite original not AI).
